sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
தஞ்சம் என்று வந்தேன் கற்பகமே
நெஞ்சம் நெகிழ அபயஹஸ்தம் தருவாய்
sections.translit:
thanjam endRu vandhEn kaRpagamE
nenjam negizha abayahastham tharuvAy
sections.en: I came to seek refuge in you, Goddess Karpagambika. Please offer me your blessings with a compassionate heart.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
கறைகண்டன் கனிவோடு காணும் கல்யாணியே
கரைந்தே உருகி தீனரை ஆதரிப்பாய்
sections.translit:
kaRaikaNtan kanivOdu kANum kalyANiyE
karaindhE urugi dhInarai AdharippAy
sections.en: You are the auspicious one whom Lord Siva looks at with love. Your darling Siva got his neck stained blue when he drank poison to save the universe.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
மாமயிலாய் வந்த மாதவன் சோதரியே
மாமணிகள் அறுபத்து மூவரும் பணிந்த
மானவர் பாலினியே ஆம்பல் மலர்
மாவெழில் மயிலையின் மாதுமை மாண்பே
sections.translit:
mAmayilAy vandha mAdhavan sOdhariyE
mAmaNigaL aRupatthu mUvarum paNindha
mAnavar pAliniyE Ambal malar
mAvezhil mayilaiyin mAdhumai mANbE
sections.en: You, the sister of Madhava, came as a peacock to this sacred shrine. You are the goddess that the sixty-three Saivite saints worshipped and the protector of all celestial beings. You are the great Goddess Uma of Mylapore, that picturesque town where water-lilies bloom.

notes: The charanam of this song tells the story of Goddess Uma coming to earth as a peacock in present-day Mylapore. The sthalapuranam of Kapaleeswarar temple in Mylapore provides details about Devi’s arrival in Mylapore and about Lord Siva coming to marry her as Karpagavalli. Kapaleeswarar Temple Sthalapuranam
